title: Bold Conjectures, Volume I
author: Logan Chipkin (editor)
openingText: Physicist and philosopher David Deutsch’s two books, The Fabric of Reality and The Beginning of Infinity, offer a deep and coherent worldview that has improved on humanity’s ideas in physics, epistemology, morality, aesthetics, and other fundamental domains of knowledge. He’s been interviewed over one-hundred times during his career, giving his readers hours of additional content that elucidates and expands upon the ideas in his books, in addition to ideas far afield from his writings.
about:
Bold Conjectures, Volume I collects transcripts of fourteen interviews with the Oxford physicist and philosopher David Deutsch, recorded between 2012 and 2024 and edited by Logan Chipkin. The interviewers include Robert Lawrence Kuhn of Closer To Truth, the economist Tyler Cowen, the physicist Sean Carroll, the investor Naval Ravikant, the science journalist John Horgan and the philosopher Peter Boghossian, along with podcasters and students of Deutsch's work.

Each transcript opens with a table of episode details, usually with a short list of the main ideas and a list of topics, and then gives the conversation with timestamps. The subjects range across Deutsch's two books, The Fabric of Reality and The Beginning of Infinity: the many-worlds interpretation of quantum theory, constructor theory, Karl Popper's theory of knowledge, explanation and truth, artificial general intelligence, free will, optimism, education and Taking Children Seriously, and politics.

The interviews run roughly in date order, so the volume shows Deutsch's positions being tested against very different interlocutors. Chipkin's preface warns that these are transcriptions of unscripted speech and that some of Deutsch's views, for instance on free will, time travel and constructor theory, have since changed. Read the chapters in any order, as a companion to Deutsch's books or as an introduction to them.

whyItMatters.title: Ideas under live questioning
whyItMatters.body:
A book can choose its objections; an interview cannot. Here Deutsch answers sceptical, friendly and puzzled questioners in real time, and the transcripts keep the follow-ups and the moments where a question is reframed.

Today: Long-form interviews are now a main route by which ideas reach the public, and this book reads them closely.

whyItMatters.title: The many-worlds view from its leading advocate
whyItMatters.body:
Several conversations deal with the multiverse: why Deutsch regards the Everett interpretation as the plain reading of quantum theory, how universes differentiate, and what this means for time and probability. The nine Closer To Truth episodes give a compact version and the Sean Carroll and Tyler Cowen interviews take it further.

Today: The interpretation of quantum mechanics remains unsettled among physicists.

whyItMatters.title: One theory of knowledge applied everywhere
whyItMatters.body:
Across the interviews Deutsch applies Popper's view that knowledge grows by conjecture and criticism to science, mathematics, morality, artificial intelligence, child-rearing and politics. Reading them together shows how far one epistemology is made to reach.

Today: The chapters on AGI address questions now asked about large language models.

angleCards.title: Track one idea
angleCards.text: Pick a theme, such as free will, AGI or good explanations, and follow how Deutsch states it across interviews more than a decade apart.
angleCards.angleObjective: I want to follow one of David Deutsch's ideas through Bold Conjectures, Volume I and notice how his explanation of it changes between interviewers and over time.

angleCards.title: Read the questioners
angleCards.text: Notice how a cosmologist, an economist, an investor and a philosopher each push Deutsch in a different direction, and which objections he finds hardest.
angleCards.angleObjective: I want to compare how different interviewers in Bold Conjectures, Volume I challenge David Deutsch and how he responds to the strongest objections.

angleCards.title: Quantum foundations first
angleCards.text: Start with the nine Closer To Truth episodes on the multiverse, then the conversations with Charles Bédard and Sean Carroll on computation and many-worlds.
angleCards.angleObjective: I want to understand David Deutsch's view of quantum theory and the multiverse through the physics-focused interviews in Bold Conjectures, Volume I.

angleCards.title: Companion to his books
angleCards.text: Read alongside The Fabric of Reality or The Beginning of Infinity, and note where the interviews clarify, extend or revise a chapter.
angleCards.angleObjective: I want to use Bold Conjectures, Volume I as a companion to David Deutsch's books, noting where the interviews clarify or revise his published arguments.

cast.name: David Deutsch
cast.description: Oxford physicist and philosopher, author of The Fabric of Reality and The Beginning of Infinity, a pioneer of quantum computation and co-originator of constructor theory. He has been interviewed more than one hundred times; this volume transcribes over a dozen of those conversations.

cast.name: Logan Chipkin
cast.description: President and Cofounder of Conjecture Institute. He selected and edited the transcripts, wrote the preface, and is himself the interviewer in the 2020 conversation on constructor theory's application to information theory.

cast.name: Robert Lawrence Kuhn
cast.description: Creator, executive producer, writer and host of the PBS series Closer To Truth. His nine short episodes, recorded in a single session and first released in 2012, open the book with questions about quantum theory, ultimate reality and truth.

cast.name: Tyler Cowen
cast.description: American economist and columnist. His 2021 conversation, 'Multiple Worlds and Our Place in Them', ranges from decision theory in the multiverse to democracy and the risks of AGI.

cast.name: Sean Carroll
cast.description: Physicist and host of the Mindscape podcast. The 2023 conversation covers the history of the many-worlds theory, constructor theory, explanatory knowledge and complexity.

cast.name: Naval Ravikant
cast.description: Entrepreneur and investor, co-founder of AngelList. His two 2023 conversations on knowledge creation and the human race, the second joined by Brett Hall, deal with creativity, good explanations, AGI and the Enlightenment.

cast.name: John Horgan
cast.description: Science journalist and former Scientific American staff writer, author of The End of Science. His 2018 conversation questions Deutsch's optimism about unlimited scientific progress.

cast.name: Peter Boghossian
cast.description: Philosopher and host of Conversations with Peter Boghossian. The 2024 conversation, with Reid Nicewonder, covers the Fermi paradox, ideological contagion, education and coercion.

cast.name: Other interviewers
cast.description: Micah Redding (Christian Transhumanist Association, 2017), Bruce Nielson and Sadia Naeem (Theory of Anything, 2021), Sam Kuypers and Liberty Fitz-Claridge (Oxford Karl Popper Society, 2021), Allison Duettmann and Beatrice Erkers (Existential Hope, 2023), Charles Bédard (computation and mathematics, 2023) and Arjun Khemani (2024).
